decision: per-claim random lease fencing token for authenticated distributed worker mutations
scope: distributed lab workers and future Qubes qrexec workers
winner: worker identity plus per-claim leaseToken, enforced on authenticated heartbeat/complete/fail

comparison.correctness: low-medium: rejects different workers but cannot distinguish an old process from a new lease using the same stable worker identity
comparison.robustness: low after lease expiry/reclaim or process replacement

comparison.correctness: high for coordinator-owned mission state: each claim generation receives a distinct capability token and stale generations are rejected
comparison.robustness: high across lease expiry/reclaim and stable worker identity reuse; running-token state is cleared on recovery/requeue
comparison.latency: negligible local equality check; no extra network round trip
comparison.resourceUse: one UUID-sized token per claimed mission
comparison.regressionRisk: moderate and bounded: enforced only when requireLeaseToken is enabled; authenticated coordinator enables it by default while legacy in-process tests remain compatible
comparison.qa: same-worker reclaim regression, missing-token rejection, stale-token rejection, authenticated crash/retry replay with original token

comparison.robustness: high if all side effects participate in the same fencing authority
comparison.latency: higher due to external transactional service
comparison.regressionRisk: high before single-coordinator Qubes transport is proven
comparison.qa: would require external service and distributed failure matrix

whyItWon: It closes the concrete stale-worker gap with almost no runtime cost and without adding infrastructure. A worker that is restarted or loses its lease cannot complete with an old claim token even when it reuses the same workerId. The authenticated qrexec/process boundary enforces the token, while internal compatibility is preserved until all local callers migrate.
failuresAndLessons: worker identity is not a lease generation; stable worker names can be reused after restart
request HMAC authentication proves message authenticity but does not prove the sender still owns the current mission lease
fencing the coordinator state does not fence an external side effect by itself; future real side-effect adapters must carry the lease generation/idempotency key to the downstream system
completed-response replay must retain and require the original lease token so retries remain idempotent without accepting a different lease generation
